turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess the main reason I came in today is that I just... I get pulled off track so incredibly easily, and it's getting really frustrating to deal with. 

Like, I'm working on my bachelor's right now, and I'll sit down to work on something with every intention of just getting it done. I'll have my laptop open, my notes out, I'll be totally ready to go, but then... it's like the absolute tiniest thing will completely derail me. Just one Slack ping from a classmate, or honestly, even just a song lyric if I have music playing in the background to try and focus. I'll hear a specific lyric and suddenly I'm thinking about what it means, or I'll just get this completely random idea for another project that has absolutely nothing to do with what I'm currently doing. 

And then, I don't know, an hour goes by, and I'm deep down some internet rabbit hole, and suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of the data dashboard I was actually supposed to be finishing. It happens constantly. I'll just completely forget what my original train of thought even was because my brain just jumps to the next interesting thing, and I end up with all these half-finished tasks. It takes me forever to force myself back to the original assignment. So I just felt like I needed to talk to someone about it, because my friends don't seem to get derailed this easily, and it's making my coursework a lot harder and more stressful than it probably needs to be.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes an inability to sustain attention on coursework, stating they lose the thread of their work and struggle to force themselves back to the assignment.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient mentions failing to finish schoolwork, specifically noting they end up with 'all these half-finished tasks' and fail to finish the data dashboard they were supposed to complete.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly states they are easily derailed by extraneous stimuli like Slack pings and song lyrics, as well as unrelated thoughts like random ideas for other projects.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your time in grade school or middle school, did you experience these same struggles with staying on task and getting easily distracted back then?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, definitely. It's actually kind of funny you ask that because my mom is one of those people who kept all my old report cards and progress reports in this big plastic bin in the basement, and we were looking at them recently. And honestly, even way back in elementary school, it was the exact same story. 

My teachers were always writing these long comments in the margins about my behavior. They'd always say I was rushing through my worksheets. I think I just wanted to be done so I could move on to something more interesting, so I'd just speed through them as fast as humanly possible. And they were always noting that I was losing track of directions. Like, the teacher would stand at the front of the room and give us three simple steps to follow, and by the time she finished the second step, my brain was just... gone. I was looking at a bird outside or something, and I’d have to lean over and ask the kid next to me what we were actually supposed to be doing. Plus, whenever we had group work, which was a lot in elementary school, I would get so caught up in whatever thought popped into my head that I was constantly talking over my classmates. I just couldn't seem to hold the thought in and wait my turn to speak, which I know probably annoyed the other kids a lot.

And then doing homework at home... oh my gosh, homework was a whole massive production at my house. My parents literally had to take turns physically sitting right beside me at the kitchen table every single afternoon. If they didn't sit right there and basically guard me, I would just wander off. I'd get up to get a glass of water and end up in the living room playing with the dog, or I'd start my math homework, get bored after two questions, and pull out my spelling words instead. I was always starting something else before finishing the first thing. 

So, yeah, it's been happening for as long as I can remember, honestly. It's just that back then, my parents were there to force me back to my chair and make me finish, and now that I'm in college, I don't have anyone doing that for me, so the wandering off is just completely unchecked.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes getting bored after two math questions and switching to spelling, showing difficulty sustaining attention on tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient notes that when the teacher gave instructions directly, their brain would be 'gone' by the second step.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient mentions losing track of directions and always starting something else before finishing their homework.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as looking at a bird outside or getting distracted by the dog while getting water.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they would wander off and get up from their chair during homework unless their parents guarded them.
symptom_reasoning.S017: The patient explicitly states they could not hold their thoughts in and wait their turn to speak.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits to constantly talking over classmates during group work, interrupting others.
